overclaims: SayCan's own paper documents recurring failures with negation and ambiguous references.
checks.note: The excerpt, proposition, axis and outcome are all correct. The problem is e1. The cited text supports only one point: vanilla SayCan does not handle negation, and chain-of-thought prompting improved this. Nothing in the excerpt or context mentions ambiguous references or shows the failures were 'recurring'. Yet both the rationale and e1's explanation claim both. The shortened e1 excerpt also cuts 'One limitation of vanilla SayCan is that', which hides that the limitation applies to the vanilla setup.
